evidence_items.publisher: Ian R. McKenzie and colleagues, arXiv
evidence_items.explanation: The study documents tasks where increasing scale worsened performance despite broader gains in prediction and other tasks. It also reports exceptions and trend reversals, so it does not establish that scaling generally fails.

evidence_items.publisher: Hugo Touvron and colleagues, Meta, arXiv
evidence_items.explanation: The model report acknowledges remaining harmful outputs after mitigation, and the same section describes factuality limitations. These disclosures are inconsistent with general behavioral assurance.

Anthropic reported practical capability gains and improved safety measurements. These qualify any suggestion of no progress, but the announcement does not isolate scaling as their cause or establish a guarantee.

unresolved_gaps: The evidence does not enumerate every deployed model or every possible restricted application.
Commercial model comparisons do not isolate the contribution of parameter count.
